summary: Across the 52 stories Miqyas tracked from November 7 to 13, social coverage carried the heaviest negative share (13 stories, 25.0%), ahead of economic (19.2%) and political (15.4%). Most of that weight came from security and infrastructure rather than social policy: the ambush near Kohat in which KP Police said 10 personnel were killed, the shooting of two officers in Swabi, ISPR-reported operations against militant hideouts in North Waziristan, and three separate reports on the rock mass collapse and flooding at the Tarbela Dam site, which also dragged on the economic readings. Social was at the same time the most positive category (11 stories, 21.2%), helped by items such as Pakistan's first astronaut heading to the Chinese space station and two rounds of fuel price cuts late in the week, so the picture was polarised rather than uniformly bleak.

The week's clearest storyline was security in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has been under governor's rule since October 11. On November 8 the provincial home secretary announced faceless anti-terrorism courts and Rs70 billion for the CTD and police over a year, citing a shortfall of more than 10,000 police; within days came the Kohat and Swabi attacks, alongside a repelled vehicle-bomb assault on a Dera Ismail Khan police station that police reported. Officials at the briefing blamed past provincial leadership for weak ownership of counterterrorism, a claim the report carried without a PTI response. Running in parallel was a sharpening government-opposition contest: the TTAP alliance hinted at a protest movement it hopes JUI-F chief Fazlur Rehman will lead and voiced opposition to governor's rule in KP, demanded talks in Azad Jammu and Kashmir after saying police stopped its delegation, and PTI accused the government of defying a Supreme Court order over Imran Khan's hospital care, which the information minister answered by citing security concerns about PTI workers.

Economic negatives were scattered rather than tied to a single shock. They included a report that development spending has stalled despite a fiscal surplus, a study claiming the 9pm shop-closing rule cut daily customer transactions by 42 percent, the FCC dismissing pleas for review of the super tax order, the Tarbela damage, and a prolonged Microsoft outage that disrupted businesses and governments. Against these sat a new auto policy aimed at cheaper vehicles and EVs, the postponement of an LPG strike after talks, a report on foreign investors drawn by high returns, and the fuel price cuts, leaving the category mostly neutral (67.3%) with negatives (10) narrowly outnumbering positives (7).

On political lean, 47 of 52 stories were rated balanced, with four leaning pro-government and one pro-opposition. In each of the clearest cases the lean reflected sourcing gaps rather than slanted language: the KP counterterrorism briefing relied entirely on official claims, while the AJK report relayed only the opposition alliance's account with no government response. A notable pattern is that the eight stories rated politically negative were exactly the eight flagged for review, and every one of them was scored medium confidence, typically because it rested on a single official statement or an unanswered allegation. No story was rated low confidence, and the share of high-confidence readings climbed through the week, from 1 of 7 stories on November 7 to 6 of 8 on November 13 (25 high and 27 medium overall).

notableStories.headline: President, PM condole martyrdom of 10 policemen in Kohat, vow to continue fight against terrorism
notableStories.context: The deadliest single incident of the week: KP Police said 10 personnel, including a DSP, were killed in an ambush near Kohat that police blamed on the TTP, in a province already under governor's rule.

notableStories.headline: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of initiatives against terrorism
notableStories.context: Sets out the province's official counterterrorism response, including identity-shielded courts, a Rs70 billion security outlay and an acknowledged police shortfall of over 10,000, days before the Kohat and Swabi attacks.

notableStories.headline: Opposition alliance hints at movement against govt, hopes JUI-F chief will lead the effort
notableStories.context: Signals a possible escalation from parliamentary opposition to street protest, with TTAP seeking Fazlur Rehman as its leader and planning a multiparty conference first.

notableStories.headline: PTI founder Imran Khan brought to Pims, undergoes eye procedure
notableStories.context: A routine medical visit that reopened a dispute over compliance with an August Supreme Court order, with PTI and the information minister giving opposing accounts.

notableStories.headline: Opposition demands 'return to talks' in AJK
notableStories.context: Points to continuing unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir, where the opposition alliance alleges excessive force against protesters; the report carries no official response, so its claims remain unverified.
